04:44 Let's talk about biceps and triceps. The biceps actually have multiple functions, but the primary one is to bring the wrist toward the shoulder, like contract the biceps. But the other one, it's called supinate or turn the pinky out this way.
05:00 OK, that's the other thing that contracts the biceps further. And the other one is to slightly lift the shoulder, think pinkies higher than thumbs. And that can be accomplished with a barbell.

05:11 You could imagine getting all three of those movements, of bringing the wrist toward the shoulder, right? And lifting the shoulder a little bit, but then it's hard you can't turn the bar, right?
05:23 But with dumbbells, you can really get all three of those movements. Bring the wrist toward the shoulder to supinate.

05:34 Get that pinky, think higher or sort of away from the midline, this is your midline, the center of your body, away from the midline and then the shoulder lifts a little bit. So some people will opt to do this, right?

05:45 Other people will opt to do them alternating, like so. Makes it, in my opinion, easier to contract the muscle really hard, which is what you want. The downside is the other one is typically resting while you're doing this one, right.

05:58 it's hanging there passively. So, any number of these different variations will work. Straight bar, curly bar, what's called the easy bar [EZ bar], thick bar, thin bar, tons of variations. Most people, it seems, end up doing bicep curls with dumbbells.

06:16 So this is a so-called preacher curl machine. It's an isolation movement because the only joint that moves is going to be the elbow joint. You would lift the weight just a tiny bit, that's always the starting position.
06:27 That's what's going to be safest because, you know you have it under control. And then you would go through your repetitions until you reach failure. This obviously isn't the work set.

06:37 One important point is, let's say you get to here and you cannot move the weight anymore, some people will just let the weight drop back like so by straightening their arm all the way out. You can really strain something or even tear a bicep.

06:51 I've seen that there are plenty of videos of that online. Better to just stand up out of the chair, set it down, save that last centimeter of that rep for someone else. You're not doing yourself any disservice.
07:03 In fact, you're just protecting yourself against injury.

07:06 Arms day, of course, includes training your triceps, which as the name suggests, has three different heads. So for me, the dips that I do on chest and back day leave my triceps feeling like they've done some real work.
07:20 So when I come around to shoulders and arms day, I'm really trying to target the triceps directly, but I don't need to do too much more. Some people may need much more tricep development.

07:30 There are two ways that I tend to target the triceps, one is a compound movement, one is an isolation movement. Keep in mind there are lots of different ways that you could do what I'm going to describe.

07:40 But the first one, the compound movement, is an overhead movement where there's [the] long head of the triceps gets a really good stretch.

07:45 If you ever played soccer, think about throwing the soccer ball back into play from the side of the field, this kind of thing. The shoulders are going to move a bit and the elbows a bit, compound movement.

07:55 What I really like is if you have access to a cable machine, you can set the cable above you and behind you. Depending on how far away I stand from the machine, I can get a nice stretch on that long head of the triceps.

08:11 I'll lock my lat, so I'm in position, lock my core and just-- So the movement looks like it's only at the elbow, but as the set gets harder, I'll allow my shoulders to come back a bit, making sure that I still have a stretch.

08:23 I'm not setting the weight down, that's the weight down. The beginning of the movement is here, so there's a nice stretch on the triceps. So there is some shoulder movement here, so it's a bit of a compound movement.
08:33 And I will take those sets-- usually we'll do three sets to failure or somewhere close to failure in the rep range that I'm trying to target.
